newsitem.title: USA: Clinton gives support to child buckle-up campaign.
newsitem.headline: Clinton gives support to child buckle-up campaign.

text.p: President Clinton on Wednesday gave his backing to an effort by the Air Bag Safety campaign and state and city officials to step up enforcement of child car passenger safety laws.
"We know enforcement will increase seat belt and child safety seat use, so we must support law enforcement in its efforts," Clinton said in a statement.
He said "I want to applaud the campaign on this important initiative, and I pledge the administration's support."
Police in all 50 states have agreed to toughen enforcement of child passenger safety and safety belt laws during Buckle Up America Week May 19-26 and beyond, the campaign said.

The Campaign also said it wanted tougher laws to protect children, saying many laws now only cover children up to four or five years of age riding in the front seat, allowing older ones and those in the back seat to ride unrestrained.

National Highway Traffic Safety Administrator Ricardo Martinez said motor vehicles are the leading cause of death among childen, and unbuckled or improperly restrained children are at twice the risk from death or injury in a crash.
He said that more than 1,400 children die and 280,000 are injured each year as occupants in motor vehicle crashes.
